# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.

Follow [bootstrap.md](../../../../bootstrap.md) — canonical there, and idempotent by design. Under the
vendored mount it is: fetch the canon once (the one network moment), `--init` the pack
declaration + run the adoption interview, vendor the snapshot into tracked
`.claudinite/shared/` (`vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` — whole-set + stamp), track it, register the
single SessionStart orchestrator plus the Stop/PreToolUse hooks at their `shared/` paths, wire the
world- and work-scope sweeps into the project's test/CI flow (a `check_the_world.mjs` step for the
tree and a `ci-work-scope.mjs` step for the change — adding a minimal flow if the repo has none;
the Stop hook runs the work scope too, but only where a session runs), open the
maintenance-enrollment issue, categorize the project, and land the sweep green.
=== catalog ===

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core-declared` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `rules-index-current` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `claudinite-isolation` | high | complexity | check: blocking |
| `conformance-workflow` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `scheduler-workflow-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-declaration-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-declaration-matches-folder` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-phase-discipline` | medium | complexity | check: advisory |

What goes wrong when one fires:

- `core-declared` — this pack's entry is gone from `.claudinite-checks.json`, so none of the rules above run and the session cannot tell.
- `rules-index-current` — the generated index is missing, stale or unimported: the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session.
- `claudinite-isolation` — the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` [barrier](../barriers/README.md) edge).
- `conformance-workflow` — nothing in CI runs the world sweep unfiltered on a pull request, so conformance is ungated and the maintenance PR never lands.
- `scheduler-workflow-shape` — the vendored scheduler's cron, concurrency or dispatch guard has drifted: staggering, double-run safety or manual runs break.
- `task-declaration-shape` — a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal, so the task never fires or fires wrong.
- `task-declaration-matches-folder` — a declaration disagrees with its folder: discovery drops it into `errors` and every run keeps reporting healthy without it.

input.body:
Follows #939 and #966, which put the work-scope sweep into the **canon's** CI. Every member still gates only the world scope.

The two scopes answer different questions, and the tree sweep cannot stand in for the other: a version number is always present in `pack.mjs`, so only the diff says whether *this* change moved it. Same shape for every commit-scoped rule — the issue reference, an introduced merge commit, a contract change that owes a migration. Until now the work scope ran at a session's Stop hook and nowhere else, so it was enforced where a session happened to be: an unattended commit, a hand-pushed branch, or a hook that never fired reached `main` unjudged.

## What a member needs

One step beside the world sweep. The recipe must **not** be copied into every member's workflow — three parts of it are the difference between a gate and a green light, and all three want to converge centrally:

- **the base ref** — a CI checkout carries none, and a work scope with no base is an empty diff that passes every rule silently;
- **an empty scope** — the runner is as silent about judging nothing as about a clean sweep;
- **the `claudinite/…` skip** — the engine's own update and maintenance PRs have no session and no issue behind them, and their auto-merge is a queue for checks, so a red check there does not annoy anyone: it stops the repo updating, quietly and permanently.

So the logic lives in the engine tree (which vendors wholesale on every converge) as `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`, and a member carries only the invocation.

## Delivery

Advisory check (`conformance-work-scope`, core), so no member turns red on its next update — the same staging the world-scope rule used. Bootstrap Part 8 and the adoption skill wire both sweeps for new adoptions; existing members get the advisory finding with the one-line remedy.

Promotion to blocking is a later, separate call once the fleet carries the step.

Closes #976. Follows #966, which put the work sweep in the canon's own CI.

## The carrier decides the design

A member's `.github/workflows/` is member-owned and nothing converges it, so the standing rule applies: ask what carries a contract across the fleet before tightening one. What *does* converge, wholesale, on every single converge, is the **engine tree** — so the recipe goes there and members carry an invocation that never changes.

**New: `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`** — the work scope's CI entry point, the counterpart to `check_the_world.mjs`. It owns the three things that separate a gate from a green light, each of which was a way to look green while judging nothing:

| | why it exists |
|---|---|
| fetches the base ref | a CI checkout carries none, and a baseless work scope is an empty diff that passes every rule |
| refuses an empty scope | the runner is as silent about judging nothing as about a clean sweep |
| skips `claudinite/…` branches | the engine's own update/maintenance PRs have no session and no issue; their auto-merge is a queue for checks, so a red check there stops the repo updating rather than annoying anyone |

Every outcome prints why, and the runner's verdict becomes the exit code.

**The canon now runs that same entry point** — the inline bash #966 added is gone. Two spellings of one protocol in two trees is precisely the drift #801/#907/#929 were made of.

## What members get

- **`conformance-work-scope`** (core, **advisory**) — fires on a member whose CI gates the tree on every PR but runs no work sweep, with the one-line remedy. Advisory for the reason its sibling `conformance-workflow` is: a requirement added with no path to comply first is the #555 failure. Inert without a mount, and inert on a mount that predates the entry point — never a finding nobody can act on. A project that wires its sweeps into a `make` target or npm script satisfies it too.
- **bootstrap Part 8** now wires both sweeps (it previously said, in as many words, that only the world sweep belongs in CI), plus the `fetch-depth: 0` note the work sweep needs.
- **adopt-claudinite** follows.
- `core` bumped 3 → 4 so the pack actually ships — enforced now by `pack-version-bumped` from #965.

## Proof

`engine-tests/ci-work-scope.test.mjs` covers all four outcomes by **exit code and printed line**, including a fixture whose local pack always fires, proving a blocking finding reaches the exit code rather than being swallowed. `packs-tests/core/conformance-work-scope.test.mjs` covers the rule, including both inert cases; seen failing before it passed. Full suite green (2110), both sweeps clean on this change.

## Not in this PR

Promotion to blocking, and forcing delivery to the fleet — say the word and I'll drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow` and report per member.

Closes #976. Follows [#966](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/966), which put the work sweep in the canon's own CI.

## The carrier decides the design

A member's `.github/workflows/` is member-owned and nothing converges it, so the standing rule applies: ask what carries a contract across the fleet before tightening one. What *does* converge, wholesale, on every converge, is the **engine tree** — so the recipe goes there and members carry an invocation that never changes.

**New: `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`** — the work scope's CI entry point, the counterpart to `check_the_world.mjs`. It owns the three things that separate a gate from a green light, each a way to look green while judging nothing:

| | why it exists |
|---|---|
| fetches the base ref | a CI checkout carries none, and a baseless work scope is an empty diff that passes every rule |
| refuses an empty scope | the runner is as silent about judging nothing as about a clean sweep |
| skips `claudinite/…` branches | the engine's own update/maintenance PRs have no session and no issue; their auto-merge is a queue for checks, so a red check there stops the repo updating rather than annoying anyone |

Every outcome prints why, and the runner's verdict becomes the exit code.

**The canon now runs that same entry point** — the inline bash #966 added is gone. Two spellings of one protocol in two trees is precisely the drift #801/#907/#929 were made of.

## What members get

- **`conformance-work-scope`** (core, **advisory**) — fires on a member whose CI gates the tree on every PR but runs no work sweep, with the one-line remedy. Advisory for the reason its sibling `conformance-workflow` is: a requirement added with no path to comply first is the #555 failure. Inert without a mount, and inert on a mount that predates the entry point — never a finding nobody can act on. A project that wires its sweeps into a `make` target or npm script satisfies it too.
- **bootstrap Part 8** now wires both sweeps (it previously said, in as many words, that only the world sweep belongs in CI), plus the `fetch-depth: 0` note the work sweep needs.
- **adopt-claudinite** follows.
